key_insight: Remanent strain-induced line defects and fracture-related disorder in magnetite do not measurably shift or broaden the Verwey transition, unlike point defects.
engineering_relevance: Plastic deformation can leave substantial structural damage without degrading this key electronic phase transition, helping distinguish when defect engineering matters for magnetite performance.
method: Dark-field x-ray microscopy (DFXM) to image remanent defects and strain fields
Ac magnetic susceptibility to track the Verwey transition temperature and sharpness
Compare uniaxial compression cases: stable plasticity, fracture, and a separate [001] loading geometry
evidence_signal: Across compressed and fractured single-crystal samples, real-space, orientation, and residual-strain maps showed strong damage, yet the measured Verwey transition temperature and sharpness remained essentially unchanged.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on specific loading directions and stoichiometric single crystals, so the result may not generalize to all stress states, compositions, or defect types.
paper_title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
